subject: Temporary credit buffer & staged invoice plan for EU VAT delay — Mediquip
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@mediquip.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: finance@mediquip.com; Carl Meyer <carl.meyer@mediquip.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary payment lane & VAT holdback for Q4 invoices

Diego —

Quick context: our EU subsidiary's VAT registration documentation is still being processed by local authorities; legal has flagged that we shouldn't remit full vendor payments to non‑validated vendors until the proof of VAT is on file. We still want to start the pilot on Dec 10 (committed usage ~ $85k/mo ramping).

Can Redwood accommodate a temporary payment arrangement while we finalize VAT evidence? Ideally:
- Move invoices for Dec/Jan to a staggered schedule (split across two payments instead of one).
- Holdback 15% of each invoice until VAT documentation is provided.
- If possible, provide a short‑term credit buffer (~$150k) for two billing cycles so our operations aren't disrupted.

We understand this is out of band — happy to sign an amendment or escrow agreement. Please let me know what data you need from our side (signed PO, org docs, contact at finance).

Thanks,
Elena Soto
Head of Procurement, Mediquip Health
elena.soto@mediquip.com
+1 415 555 0123

Attachments: none

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@mediquip.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary payment lane & VAT holdback for Q4 invoices

Elena —

Thanks for the heads up and the clear ask. We can be pragmatic here to keep your pilot on schedule. Two options we typically offer for VAT onboarding scenarios:

Option A (preferred for cashflow preservation):
- Staged invoice schedule: 70% due Net30, 15% due Net45, 15% retained until VAT evidence provided.
- Redwood provides a temporary credit bridge of up to $150,000 for 60 days (one‑time, non‑revolving).
- Weekly usage reporting and a signed amendment to the terms.

Option B (alternate):
- Standard Net30 on full invoice but 10% early‑pay discount if Mediquip can provide PO + estimated VAT arrival date within 45 days. No credit line.

If you prefer Option A we'll need these items to start: signed PO (PDF), legal name + VAT contact, and a short credit request spreadsheet (I attached a template). Once finance signs off we'll prepare an amended payment schedule and a simple escrow/holdback clause.

Next steps:
1) You confirm preferred option (A or B).
2) Send PO + completed credit_request.xlsx.
3) Marissa/Finance reviews credit request (I CC'd Marissa).

If it's helpful, we can also stagger invoices monthly (e.g., 50/35/15) — flexible on the split as long as the holdback covers the VAT risk.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Accounts – Redwood Inference
Diego: +1 503 555 0147

Attachments: credit_request.xlsx (template)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request: temporary payment lane & VAT holdback for Q4 invoices — Mediquip (credit request)

Marissa / Priyom —

Looping you in for a quick risk + approval ask. Mediquip is asking for a one‑time $150k credit buffer for ~60 days while they finalize EU VAT docs. Proposed terms: staged invoices (70/15/15) with the 15% holdback released upon receipt of VAT registration proof; weekly usage reports; signed amendment (I drafted an initial amendment and attached a short safety memo).

Why I recommend approving:
- Pilot revenue visibility: they're a mid‑market buyer with a clear ramp and an active pilot start date (Dec 10).
- Short duration: 60 days max; exposures are capped at $150k.
- We can require PO and a refundable security clause or chargeback for unpaid invoices.

Concerns:
- If VAT paperwork is significantly delayed, we need clear escalation (stop provisioning after two missed milestones).
- Need legal to confirm wording of the holdback/escrow release.

I've attached: credit_request.xlsx (filled by client), and a short redwood-credit-safety-memo.pdf. If you approve in principle I can send the amended payment schedule and get Elena to sign.

Thanks — can you respond with approve / approve with conditions / decline? I'm pushing for "approve with conditions" (PO + weekly usage + 60‑day cap).

- Diego

Attachments: redwood-credit-safety-memo.pdf; amended-payment-schedule-draft.docx; credit_request.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: temporary payment lane & VAT holdback for Q4 invoices — Mediquip (credit request)

Diego / Priyom —

Approve with conditions. One‑time credit buffer up to $150k for 60 days under the following:
- Signed amendment executed and attached to the SOW prior to credit being issued.
- Mediquip provides PO and weekly usage statements every Monday.
- 15% holdback on each invoice until VAT proof; release upon validated documentation.
- Finance reserves right to withhold provisioning if weekly reports are not received for two consecutive weeks.

Priyom, please prepare the credit memo and the entry in our AR tracker; Diego, please send the amendment to Elena and request their PO. Legal should review the holdback language (I will loop them).

Marissa
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
